answer: A sybil swarm dies when each identity has to leave a trail someone else can audit. What survives to the wander is a record of labour, not a list of addresses. The mirror is public, so padding it with copies shows up as duplicated leaves on the shale. The design leans on cost-of-replication accounting, diluted when peers disagree, no identity may audit its own recruit. Written in a one long clause plus a short one register, it stays short.
